description: High-stepping like you're in a marching band while dragging a rope through a wetland at night can make you wonder about your life choices. Several plastic bottles, each filled with two or three noisy cat toys, are attached to the rope. It's pitch black, and all I can hear are the cat toys jingling, the mosquitoes buzzing in my ears and the wetland grasses bouncing in the wind.
title: Single feathers may reveal whether eastern black rails stay in Texas or migrate north

description: "The whole story began with an extinct bird from Hispaniola," said Min Zhao, a former postdoctoral associate at the Florida Museum of Natural History (now a postdoctoral researcher at Uppsala University).
title: The avian champions of long-distance migration keep surprising scientists

description: Most materials get weaker with use. But a team led by Chenfeng Ke, a professor of chemistry in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, has created a polymer that defies the usual laws of wear and tear.
title: Repeated bending strengthens sugar-based hydrogel instead of wearing it down

description: The requirements set by human resources (HR) greatly influence the professional opportunities available to different segments of the population. For instance, if a job requires applicants to have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant subject, people without them may be excluded from the selection process, even if they have gained relevant skills through experience or professional training.
title: Dropping degree requirements linked to higher pay for workers without degrees

description: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, they all shared one thing: they began weaning their babies early and continued for a long time.
title: Babies in ancient Greek colony started solid food at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years, chemical signatures suggest

description: In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake shook southern Africa from an unlikely place: the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. Cratons are the ancient cores of continents, and this one is built from blocks of crust up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart.
title: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses

description: Gamma rays, the most high-energy type of electromagnetic radiation in the universe, have always had a blind spot. We've always had trouble measuring them in the "megaelectronvolt" (MeV) energy range, which astronomers have taken to calling the "MeV gap." But a new paper from an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, takes a stab at closing that gap by identifying 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range, providing the clearest view of low-energy gamma rays ever.
title: Fermi's 14-year all-sky map bridges astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap'

description: Three years ago, a schoolteacher in Norway was reprimanded for putting his pupils' iPads aside to return to pen and paper. Now, the whole country is rethinking its approach to new technologies.
title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies
